articles.title: César Millán, dog trainer: “Dogs know how comfortable you feel with yourself, how happy you are, how scared you are, and what is missing inside you”
articles.standfirst: Dogs are more aware than we think.
articles.summary: Dogs are more aware than we think.
articles.body:
Dogs have become very important companion animals for human beings today, who have found ways to communicate with these animals throughout history. César Millán , a dog trainer known as “The Dog Whisperer,” has shared reflections on this bond.

"The Dog Whisperer" shared this phrase on social media: “Dogs know how comfortable you feel with yourself, how happy you are, how scared you are, and what is missing inside you” . This lesson went viral among users who identified with the words written by this trainer.

That is why at MARCA we will tell you what lies behind this reflection by the dog whisperer, who became famous all over the world thanks to a television program where he shared his methods for training dogs.

What does this phrase by César Millán mean?

The phrase “Dogs know how comfortable you feel with yourself, how happy you are, how scared you are, and what is missing inside you” reflects the clear bond that exists between dogs and their owners, which can affect their mood and behavior. César Millán firmly believes that these animals are aware of the relationship they have with their owners.

In this way, the dog trainer ensures that these animals are not merely beings that accompany their owners in their daily lives, but rather that they have enough intelligence to notice changes in human beings' moods and behavior, even if they cannot express it in words.

Currently, thousands of people in Mexico have dogs , which are no longer considered pets but have come to play an important role within their families as companion animals, which is why the curious term “fur babies” has emerged, used by people who have dogs and treat them as if they were their children.

Who is César Millán, the dog whisperer?

' César Millán is a famous Mexican-American dog trainer and television host, known worldwide as "The Dog Whisperer." He was born in Culiacán, Sinaloa, on August 27, 1969.'

He currently has a ranch that serves as a rehabilitation center in California, where he helps dogs with serious behavioral problems. He has also published several books about dog training and his experiences dedicating himself to this work.

He has also had controversies, as in the past he was accused of animal abuse against some dogs.

articles.title: Who was Colleen Slemmer? The young woman brutally murdered by Christa Pike along with Tadaryl Shipp and Shadola Peterson in a macabre ritual
articles.standfirst: The death of the 19-year-old young woman shocked Tennessee in 1995 and led Christa Pike to become the only woman sentenced to death in that state
articles.summary: The death of the 19-year-old young woman shocked Tennessee in 1995 and led Christa Pike to become the only woman sentenced to death in that state
articles.body:
Colleen Slemmer was 19 years old when she was murdered on January 12, 1995 in Knoxville, Tennessee . She was a student in the Job Corps program, a job training center where Christa Pike , then 18, Tadaryl Shipp , 17, and Shadolla Peterson , 18, were also enrolled.

The crime was especially brutal and from the very first moment it was surrounded by elements that caused enormous public impact . The Tennessee courts established that Slemmer was attacked by the three youths and suffered multiple wounds before dying . The Tennessee Supreme Court's ruling described, among other facts, cuts made with a box cutter and a small butcher knife , as well as blows to the head with a rock or a piece of asphalt .

According to court documents, the confrontation was related to a romantic dispute . Prosecutors argued that Pike saw Slemmer as a rival because of her relationship with Shipp and that the group drove the young woman to a secluded area near the University of Tennessee facilities.

Beyond the shocking details of the crime, Slemmer was a 19-year-old young woman who had plans for her future . Her mother, May Martinez , has told U.S. media that her daughter volunteered at the Special Olympics , enjoyed skating, and was interested in pursuing a career related to computers.

Martinez also recalled that Slemmer had called her family on the night of her murder . The communication was interrupted due to coverage problems and, when her mother tried to call her back, the young woman had already left. In statements reported by U.S. media, Martinez has said that the memory of her daughter remains present decades after the crime .

Tennessee court records show that t he attack lasted approximately between 30 and 45 minutes . The court documentation indicates that some of the wounds were inflicted while Slemmer was still alive and that one of the most striking elements of the case was the figure of a pentagram that was marked on her chest . These details contributed to the murder being associated for years with the climate of fear surrounding the so-called "satanic panic" that had swept through the United States in previous decades .

The role of Christa Pike and her two accomplices

Pike was considered by prosecutors to be primarily responsible for the murder and, in 1996, a jury found her guilty of first-degree murder and conspiracy to commit murder. The Tennessee Supreme Court later concluded that the evidence supported a finding of premeditation and deliberation .

One of the elements that carried special weight in the process was Pike's behavior after the crime . The state Supreme Court's ruling states that she tried to hide evidence and that she later showed another person a fragment of Slemmer's skull that she had kept as a souvenir . Pike was sentenced to death and remained on Tennessee's death row for decades.

Shipp and Peterson’s fate was very different. Shipp , who was 17 years old when the murder occurred, was found guilty of first-degree murder, conspiracy, and received a life sentence, in addition to a sentence for conspiracy . Peterson pleaded guilty to being an accessory after the fact and received a six-year probation sentence after cooperating with authorities , according to Tennessee court records.

A case that returns to the headlines three decades later

The story came back into the spotlight in 2026 due to Pike's situation . The Tennessee Supreme Court had set September 30 as the date for her execution, which would have made Pike the first woman executed in Tennessee in more than two centuries. The case also drew attention because Pike was 18 years old when she committed the murder.

In the hours leading up to the execution, a new judicial chapter unfolded. A federal appeals court had temporarily halted the procedure to review issues related to Pike's allegations of sexual abuse suffered during her childhood and whether those circumstances had been adequately considered during the sentencing phase. However, the United States Supreme Court later overturned that stay and allowed the procedure to move forward , according to the high court's own ruling.

Finally, the execution did not end as planned. According to information reported by U.S. media and Pike's lawyers, she received two doses of pentobarbital during the procedure and remained alive . Press witnesses reported that she was still breathing and that they even heard her snoring before officials removed the journalists from the room. The Tennessee Department of Correction later confirmed that Pike was transferred to an external medical facility .

Tennessee Governor Bill Lee later announced the suspension of the remaining executions scheduled for 2026 and ordered an independent review of the procedure . Pike's lawyers, for their part, filed an emergency petition with the Supreme Court to halt any new execution attempt and argued that what had happened had caused unnecessary suffering .

Thus, Colleen Slemmer's name is once again at the center of public attention more than 31 years after her murder . Her story became linked to one of Tennessee's best-known criminal cases of the 1990s, while Christa Pike's legal situation remains unresolved after the failed execution attempt .

articles.title: Christa Pike survived her execution, but her sentence still stands: What will happen now?
articles.standfirst: The failed execution opened an unprecedented scenario in Tennessee. Pike remains sentenced to death, while authorities investigate what happened and uncertainty grows over whether the state will be able to try to execute her again.
articles.summary: The failed execution opened an unprecedented scenario in Tennessee. Pike remains sentenced to death, while authorities investigate what happened and uncertainty grows over whether the state will be able to try to execute her again.
articles.body:
C hrista Pike survived the execution attempt that was supposed to end her life in Tennessee, but that does not mean her sentence is behind her. The 50-year-old woman remains sentenced to death for the chilling murder of Colleen Slemmer in 1995, and now her case enters much less familiar territory: determining what will happen after the state incredibly failed to carry out her execution.

Tennessee Governor Bill Lee ordered an independent and thorough review of the procedure and suspended the remaining execution scheduled in the state for 2026 , and it is not clear whether this would include Pike's case. Authorities will have to determine what happened inside the execution chamber before deciding the next steps in a case that has already raised new legal questions.

Can they try to execute Christa Pike again?

Surviving an execution, no matter how shocking it may be, does not automatically nullify a death sentence . For the time being, there is no court ruling that has set aside Pike’s conviction, nor has the state announced a new date to execute her.

That means Tennessee could eventually try to carry out the sentence again, although any decision in that regard would likely open a new battle in the courts . Pike's lawyers could challenge another attempt based, among other arguments, on the U.S. constitutional prohibition against cruel and unusual punishments.

There is even a precedent in U.S. history. In 1946, Willie Francis survived an execution attempt in the electric chair in Louisiana. The case reached the Supreme Court, which in Louisiana ex rel. Francis v. Resweber determined that carrying out a second attempt did not violate, under those circumstances, the Constitution. Francis was executed the following year.

However, that precedent does not automatically determine what will happen with Pike. The method, the circumstances, and the legal arguments are different, and any attempt by Tennessee to set a new execution could once again be submitted to the judgment of the courts.

Tennessee investigates before deciding the next step

The Department of Corrections stated that during the procedure, the current protocol was followed , while the state tries to determine why the execution did not produce the expected result.

Among the possible explanations are several of the problems that Pike's defense had warned about. Her attorneys mentioned difficulties accessing veins, lines that may have failed, and the possibility that the pentobarbital was degraded. Specialists have also suggested that the drug may not have reached in the blood the concentration necessary to cause respiratory and cardiovascular arrest. For now, these are hypotheses: no technical analyses of the batch used have been published that would make it possible to determine what happened.

'The lawyers for the Idaho Federal Defender Services organization stated: "This is what happens when unknown people, with unknown training, are assigned to carry out an execution".'

The episode once again puts the status of the drugs used in executions under the spotlight. Restrictions imposed by manufacturers and distributors in recent years have made it harder to obtain these substances, while questions persist about the transparency and controls applied to the drugs intended for lethal injections.

Pike was supposed to become the first woman executed in Tennessee in more than 200 years. Instead, she survived the procedure and her case opened a new chapter. Her death sentence remains in force, but Tennessee must now resolve two different issues : what went wrong during the execution and, above all, whether it will try again to carry out the sentence and under what conditions it may do so.

articles.title: Donald Trump questions how Christa Pike's execution failed: "Should be easy to do"
articles.standfirst: Christa Pike survived two rounds of lethal injection, and President Donald Trump says he can't understand how it happened.
articles.summary: Christa Pike survived two rounds of lethal injection, and President Donald Trump says he can't understand how it happened.
articles.body:
President Donald Trump expressed disbelief over Christa Pike 's failed execution and wondered how it could have happened, since, in his view, administering the lethal drugs should be "easy."

Pike survived two rounds of lethal injection and became the first person in history to survive that method of execution .

"How does that happen?," Trump said. "Should be easy to do. It shouldn't be very difficult."

The president called the case "interesting" but avoided commenting on next steps, saying that decision is up to the state of Tennessee.

"That was an interesting situation, but you're going to have to speak to Tennessee about it. Whether or not they're going to go forward," he told reporters who traveled with him to Texas.

Christa Pike is still alive after the failed execution

Pike, 50, was set to become the first woman executed by the state of Tennessee in 200 years. She was convicted of torture and murder: in 1995 , when both were teenagers, she brutally beat a classmate to death and mutilated her body with a box cutter.

She is currently still alive and in critical condition.

Her attorneys said Thursday that during the failed procedure she endured at least seven attempts with needles. Randy Spivey , one of them, called what happened "cruel and torturous" and asked Tennessee Gov. Bill Lee to commute her sentence to life in prison.

Pike had asked to die by hanging

Pike had previously asked to be executed by hanging. She argued that the damaged veins in her arms would make it difficult for those carrying out the execution to access them to administer the pentobarbital.

Gov. Lee suspended all executions in Tennessee while the case is reviewed and called what happened to Pike a "tragedy."

articles.title: Christa Pike, trapped in a legal limbo after surviving her execution by lethal injection in Tennessee
articles.standfirst: The 50-year-old woman remains hospitalized in critical condition after receiving two doses of pentobarbital
articles.summary: The 50-year-old woman remains hospitalized in critical condition after receiving two doses of pentobarbital
articles.body:
c hrista Pike was supposed to become on September 30 the first woman executed in Tennessee in more than 200 years. However, the lethal injection did not end her life. The inmate, who had spent three decades on death row, received two doses of pentobarbital and continued breathing for nearly an hour, according to the documents filed by her lawyers and the journalists who witnessed the procedure.'

Christa Pike was eventually transferred to a hospital, where she remains in critical condition and receiving life-sustaining medical care, according to her legal team. Her lawyers say they still do not know what her prognosis is. The episode has created an unprecedented situation for Tennessee authorities: the execution protocol provides for a second dose if the inmate has not died after the first, but it does not specify what to do if the person remains alive after both.

Two doses and an execution that was not carried out

The procedure began on Wednesday night at the Nashville prison. Officials administered an initial dose of pentobarbital, but Christa Pike did not die. A second dose was subsequently administered. Witnesses present in the room said that Christa Pike continued breathing and making loud snoring sounds. She also reportedly moved different parts of her body and, at one point, raised her head. When the media were forced to leave the area, the woman was still alive. Shortly afterward, she was transported by ambulance to a hospital.

Her attorney Randy Spivey has sharply questioned how the procedure was carried out. According to the defense, at least seven needles were used over approximately an hour in an attempt to administer the substances, and one of them reportedly came out bent. The lawyers had previously warned about the difficulties in accessing Christa Pike's veins and the problems this method of execution could pose. The defense maintains that precisely because of this history, Christa Pike had requested that another method of execution be used. Her request was not accepted.

A case that leaves Tennessee facing an unprecedented situation

The Tennessee Department of Corrections maintains that its officials followed all the steps established in the execution protocol approved by state authorities and that the pentobarbital used had previously proven effective. The situation, however, has left an open legal question: what happens to a woman sentenced to death whose execution has not been carried out and who remains alive after receiving the prescribed doses?

The matter is now in the hands of the courts. Christa Pike's defense has filed appeals to ensure her medical care and to challenge the legal consequences of the failed procedure. Tennessee Governor Bill Lee announced the suspension of all executions scheduled in the state for the remainder of 2026 and ordered an independent review to determine exactly what happened during the procedure.

Three decades on death row

Christa Pike was sentenced to death for the 1995 murder of Colleen Slemmer, a 19-year-old student, when Christa Pike was 18. The case shocked the United States because of the brutality of the crime and the ritual elements surrounding the murder. Since then, she has spent around 30 years on death row. Her execution was scheduled for September 30, after the Supreme Court of the United States allowed the procedure to go ahead following a temporary stay by an appeals court.

Now, instead of having ended her life, the procedure has resulted in an entirely different situation: Christa Pike is fighting to survive in a hospital while the courts must determine what consequences the failed execution attempt will have. The case has once again brought the lethal injection protocols in the United States under scrutiny. In fact, Christa Pike's is not the first problematic execution in Tennessee in 2026: months earlier, the state had to abort the scheduled procedure for Tony Carruthers due to problems establishing an intravenous line.

Christa Pike's survival after receiving two doses of pentobarbital has, due to its circumstances, turned the case into an extraordinary episode in the recent history of the American death penalty and prompted a new review of the procedures used to carry out capital sentences.

articles.title: Who is Yassamin Ansari? The congresswoman who is in a relationship with a YouTuber ten years younger
articles.standfirst: The 34-year-old Democratic representative is dating 24-year-old Jack Cocchiarella
articles.summary: The 34-year-old Democratic representative is dating 24-year-old Jack Cocchiarella
articles.body:
A romantic relationship has been causing a stir in the world of American politics in recent days. TMZ has reported that progressive congresswoman Yassamin Ansari (Democrat from Arizona) is in a romantic relationship with left-wing YouTuber Jack Cocchiarella, who is ten years younger than her.

'Sources with direct knowledge have told TMZ that the two have been dating for the past few months and that the relationship is going very well. They met when Cocchiarella interviewed Ansari in the spring of 2025... they began hanging out as friends a few months later and, eventually, the relationship turned romantic," TMZ reported.'

I’m not going to comment on my personal life

After the news broke, the 34-year-old Iranian-born politician declined to confirm or deny whether she is in a relationship with the 24-year-old YouTuber.

“No comment on my personal life, nor is it anyone’s business. Right now, ICE is terrorizing communities all across the country without being held accountable to anyone, and Trump’s reckless war in Iran continues unabated,” she told TMZ.

“I’m focused on helping the House of Representatives change majority so that we can pass important laws; that’s what we should all be focused on,” she added.

articles.title: 56,000 years ago, a meteorite may have been behind the Grand Canyon of Colorado
articles.standfirst: Evidence found of two geological events that apparently had no connection
articles.summary: Evidence found of two geological events that apparently had no connection
articles.body:
There are iconic places all around the planet that people visit without ever really learning their origin, or what or how they were created. One of the best known in the United States is the Grand Canyon of Colorado and, specifically, the Barringer Crater , also known as Meteor Crater, which was formed some 56,000 years ago.

A group of scientists has shared in the journal Geology their striking breakthrough regarding the connection between two events that, apparently, had no relation and that all signs point to the fact that they did. Apparently, a 'curveball' from space pierced the Earth's surface and struck, traveling more than 160 kilometers to the Grand Canyon, causing a landslide onto the Colorado River .

“There are other possibilities, such as a random rockfall or a local earthquake occurring within the thousand years following the impact of the meteorite crater, which could have happened independently ,” explains Karl Karlstrom , professor of Earth and Planetary Sciences at the University of New Mexico.

The Grand Canyon of the Colorado: A river flood and the formation of the crater, linked in time

According to the data, it would be too much of a coincidence for two such important events to occur in such a short period and not be, as is believed, related. One piece of evidence of the flood is Stanton Cave, 46 meters above river level , which at the time revealed logs carried by the current.

“It would have required a flood ten times greater than any that had occurred in the last several thousand years,” says Karlstrom, whose analyses of the wood indicate that it was around 56,000 years old , demonstrating that both events occurred within a surprisingly short span of time. And David Kring , co-author of the study, has evidence that the Barringer Crater is the same age as that flood.

“The meteorite impact, the massive landslide, the lake deposits, and the driftwood found far above the river level are rare and unusual events ,” the experts conclude.

articles.title: Stephen Hawking, physicist: “The greatest enemy of knowledge is not ignorance, it is the illusion of knowledge”
articles.standfirst: We share Stephen Hawking's reflection on ignorance and knowledge.
articles.summary: We share Stephen Hawking's reflection on ignorance and knowledge.
articles.body:
S tephen Hawking was one of the most renowned scientists of the 20th century and a fundamental figure in the study of black holes, cosmology, and the origin of the universe. In addition to his contributions to theoretical physics, his reflections on science, learning, and the limits of knowledge continue to spark interest among students, researchers, and readers around the world.

One of the phrases attributed to him states: “The greatest enemy of knowledge is not ignorance, it is the illusion of knowledge” . This reflection invites us to think about the importance of recognizing what we know, questioning our own beliefs, and maintaining an open attitude toward the possibility of being wrong.

The phrase draws a distinction between being unaware of a subject and believing it is fully understood. While ignorance can motivate a person to investigate and learn, the false sense of knowing can prevent them from seeking new information or considering other explanations.

“What does this Stephen Hawking quote mean?”

The phrase “The greatest enemy of knowledge is not ignorance, it is the illusion of knowledge” relates to the importance of recognizing the limits of our understanding. Its main message is that a person can learn more when they admit they do not know something than when they are convinced they have all the answers.

Ignorance, understood as a lack of information about a matter, can be the starting point for investigating, asking questions, and acquiring new knowledge. In contrast, the illusion of knowledge appears when someone believes they have mastered a subject without having enough arguments, experience, or evidence to support that confidence.

For example, a person may read a headline about a scientific discovery and assume they fully understand its implications. However, knowing an isolated fact is not the same as understanding the research process, the evidence that supports it, or the limitations of its conclusions.

This difference is also observed in everyday life. When someone is convinced that they are always right, they may reject other people's opinions, ignore information that contradicts their beliefs, and stop questioning their own decisions. As a result, their opportunities to learn decrease.

The phrase attributed to Stephen Hawking therefore invites us to practice intellectual humility. This concept consists of recognizing that our knowledge is limited and that even the ideas we consider correct may need revision when new evidence appears.

Stephen Hawking was born on January 8, 1942, in Oxford, England, and died on March 14, 2018, in Cambridge. He was a British theoretical physicist, cosmologist, and science communicator who made significant contributions to the study of black holes and the universe.

He studied at the University of Oxford and later developed his academic career at the University of Cambridge, where he researched issues related to general relativity, gravity, and the origins of the cosmos. His work helped deepen understanding of some of the most complex phenomena in the universe.

articles.title: SNAP benefits: Millions lose food assistance as new rules put more recipients at risk
articles.standfirst: Expanded work requirements affect more adults and parents of teenagers
articles.summary: Expanded work requirements affect more adults and parents of teenagers
articles.body:
Losing SNAP benefits means having less money to buy groceries. About 5.2 million fewer people received food assistance in June 2026 than in July 2025 , according to a Food Research & Action Center analysis of USDA data. The decline followed the passage of a federal law that tightened eligibility rules for the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program.

For people still struggling to find work, losing assistance does not mean their financial problems have ended. Lori Covelli, an unemployed social worker in Wisconsin, told CBS News she lost her benefits while looking for a job. “It feels as though people are being punished,” she said.

Who faces SNAP’s work requirements, and how can you protect your benefits?

The law President Donald Trump signed on July 4, 2025, expanded SNAP’s additional work requirement to adults ages 18 through 64 . Parents whose youngest child is 14 through 17 may also be affected because having a teenager no longer provides the same exemption it previously did.

People subject to this rule generally must complete at least 80 hours a month of work, qualifying volunteer service, approved job training, or a combination of qualifying activities . Without meeting the requirement or qualifying for an exemption, they are generally limited to three months of SNAP benefits within a three-year period . Applying for jobs alone should not be assumed to satisfy the requirement; ask your state agency which activities count.

These requirements do not apply to everyone receiving SNAP. Exemptions include pregnancy, a physical or mental condition that prevents someone from working, and responsibility for a child younger than 14. Other exemptions may apply. If a health condition limits your ability to work, ask your SNAP office what documentation it needs to evaluate your case.

If you receive a notice reducing or ending your benefits, take these steps:

- Read the reason and deadline. Check whether the issue involves missing paperwork, renewal requirements, income, or proof of qualifying activities.

- Ask about exemptions. Explain any health limitations or caregiving responsibilities and ask what evidence the agency accepts.

- Confirm which activities count. Before starting volunteer work or a training program, ask how to document your hours.

- Request a fair hearing if you disagree. You have the right to challenge a decision about your case. Follow the notice’s appeal instructions promptly and keep copies of submitted documents.

Your state or local SNAP office handles your application and benefits , rather than USDA directly. Find its contact information through the USDA’s official state directory If your benefits have already ended, ask how to regain eligibility. Meeting the activity requirement again or establishing an exemption may allow you to qualify, provided you meet the program’s other eligibility rules.

Another change took effect on October 1, 2026: states must now cover 75% of SNAP’s administrative costs , up from 50%. That shifts more of the expense of running the program to state governments. It does not, by itself, automatically reduce the amount deposited on your EBT card.

If you need food immediately, ask whether you qualify for expedited SNAP processing . Eligible households can receive benefits within seven days of applying. You can also call the National Hunger Hotline at 1-866-348-6479 for English or 1-877-842-6273 for Spanish , Monday through Friday, from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. Eastern time , for help finding nearby food resources while your case is being resolved.

articles.title: Who was Cibelle Savella? The perpetrator of the crime that horrifies everyone because of its cruelty in Texas
articles.standfirst: Killed her 4-year-old daughter after losing custody and later took her own life
articles.summary: Killed her 4-year-old daughter after losing custody and later took her own life
articles.body:
The murder of a 4-year-old girl in Texas at the hands of her mother has shocked American society. Cibelle Savella, 35, shot and killed her daughter Vivian before handing her over to her ex-husband, Aaron Savella, according to ABC13.

Hours earlier, a judge had decided to grant custody to the father, in a decision that precipitated the tragedy in Houston. The woman, of Brazilian origin, decided to take revenge by killing her own daughter, before also taking her own life.

The couple divorced just two years ago, after only 4 years of marriage. The ruling included a ban on speaking to her daughter in her native language, Portuguese, and also on attending her daughter's extracurricular school activities. In addition, financial obligations were imposed on her regarding child support or health insurance.

'According to the father's lawyer, "the court did not specify exactly how the custody exchange was to be carried out". Something that ultimately never came to pass. The crime and subsequent suicide took place in the presence of Cibelle's current partner, Greg Kubala, and a nanny.'

“Aaron did everything the law requires of a father trying to protect his child. He trusted the courts. He followed all the orders. He waited for the process to run its course. On Tuesday, a judge placed Vivian in his custody, and she was supposed to return home with him that same night. She never did,” the girl's father stated.

articles.title: The song Christa Pike sang before escaping death and a diabolical laugh
articles.standfirst: Pike has been on death row since 1996.
articles.summary: Pike has been on death row since 1996.
articles.body:
C hrista Pike sang with her spiritual adviser and laughed during a failed execution that left her alive in a Tennessee hospital, with witnesses later describing how she appeared to fall into a deep sleep despite receiving two doses of lethal drugs. The 50-year-old killer was scheduled to be executed at Riverbend Maximum Security Institution on September 30 after spending three decades on death row for the 1995 murder of Job Corps classmate Colleen Slemmer .

Witnesses entered the execution chamber shortly before 7pm, with Pike already strapped to the gurney and an IV attached to her arm. She delivered what was expected to be her final statement before turning her attention to her spiritual adviser. “I just want to say that I’m going to leave this world the way I spent most of my life and that is with love,” Pike said, according to accounts of the execution. She added that she loved both her supporters and those who hated her, and said she is at peace. Pike then sang I Love You So Much and is reported to have smiled and laughed after complaining about a vein in her arm. Minutes later, however, the execution began to take an unexpected turn.

Pike successfully resists two fatal injections

A small white rock appeared in a window at about 7:41pm, which witnesses understood as a signal that the lethal drugs had been administered before the blinds were then closed minutes later. However, William Puckett , who watched from the observation room, said Pike was still conscious and moving after the first injection and he described hearing what he called, “a joyous laugh and chuckle.” The curtain later rose again, and witnesses could see that Pike remained alive before a second dose was administered, after which her body twitched abruptly, and she gave a significant gasp for air. The blinds were closed again at approximately 8:05pm, once again signaling the dose had been given but the sounds coming from inside the chamber suggested that the execution had still not been completed. Puckett described hearing a “loud, deep in the back of the sinus cavity snore” that sounded like an old man sleeping and the snoring continued for roughly another 50 minutes as doctors and lawyers moved in and out of the chamber. Media witnesses were eventually escorted from the building at around 8:53pm, with Pike reportedly still breathing and her attorneys later said she had maintained a heartbeat and had not lost consciousness during the attempted execution. She was transported by ambulance to a local hospital, where she remained in critical condition the following day and the failed execution has prompted further scrutiny of Tennessee ’s lethal-injection procedures. The state has halted scheduled executions in the state for the remainder of 2026 and ordered an independent review of what happened.

articles.title: Man found $128,514 sitting on an ATM. What he did next stunned the police
articles.standfirst: Information attached to one of the bags appeared to connect the cash to a nearby Chick-fil-A
articles.summary: Information attached to one of the bags appeared to connect the cash to a nearby Chick-fil-A
articles.body:
Finding a bag of cash on top of an ATM would be an unusual way to start a morning. For a 37-year-old man i n Lewisville, Texas, the discovery on Aug. 3 presented an even bigger question: What do you do when more than $128,000 is suddenly sitting in front of you? His answer was simple. He tried to find the owner.

The man, who local news outlets reported works as a barber, was at a Bank of America ATM in Lewisville, about 30 miles north of Dallas, at around 10 a.m. when he noticed a bag sitting on top of the machine. Inside was an extraordinary amount of cash. There was also a second bag containing 19 checks. Rather than leave with the money, the man began trying to determine where it came from.

He first tried to return the money himself

Information attached to one of the bags appeared to connect the cash to a nearby Chick-fil-A, according to NBC 5 and CBS News Texas, both citing Lewisville police. So the man did what many people might not have expected. He drove to the restaurant.

A manager told him the cash did not belong there. At that point, he could have simply walked away. Instead, he called 911. Lewisville police officers arrived and secured the bags while investigators began determining where the money had come from and who was responsible for it.

The investigation quickly established that this was not an ordinary lost wallet or forgotten purse. It was $128,514 in cash. Police counted the money twice Inside the cash bag, investigators found a bank receipt showing how much money was supposed to be inside.

Police counted the cash twice

They then used a digital currency counter to verify the amount, according to CBS News Texas. The result matched the amount listed on the receipt. $128,514. Not one dollar was missing. The money belonged to Bank of America and was being handled by its cash vendor, Brinks. Investigators believe a Brinks technician had serviced the ATM and accidentally left the cash bag sitting on top of the machine.

Police found no indication that the money was connected to criminal activity. Bank of America subsequently recovered the cash. The man wasn't looking for a reward and didn't ask for money in exchange for returning the cash. He also wasn't apparently looking for publicity.

His identity has not been publicly confirmed, and local reports have described him primarily as a Lewisville barber. Bank of America expressed its gratitude for his actions, according to NBC 5. For Lewisville police, however, the sheer amount of money involved made the incident unlike anything they had previously handled.

Detective Gina Miller said she has dealt with people returning lost wallets, identification and other property. But $128,514 in cash was a different story. “I've never had a case like this before, ever,” Miller said, according to CBS News Texas.

articles.title: Best Autumn Products at Costco: Every item that you can get this season at the best price
articles.standfirst: From pumpkin pie and apple cider doughnuts to Halloween candy and cozy fall meals, Costco is bringing back a wide selection of seasonal favorites in October 2026
articles.summary: From pumpkin pie and apple cider doughnuts to Halloween candy and cozy fall meals, Costco is bringing back a wide selection of seasonal favorites in October 2026
articles.body:
Autumn has arrived at Costco , and the warehouse is filling its shelves with the flavors and products shoppers associate with the season.

October's selection includes everything from pumpkin desserts and apple-inspired treats to Halloween candy, hearty prepared foods and even kitchen equipment for those already thinking about holiday entertaining.

Several of the seasonal products are limited-time offerings, meaning availability can vary by warehouse and some items may disappear before the end of fall.

One of the most recognizable returns is the Kirkland Signature Pumpkin Pie. The nearly four-pound, 58-ounce pie is selling for around $6, making it one of the more affordable ways to put a traditional fall dessert on the table.

Costco is also carrying Pumpkin Streusel Muffins, with an eight-pack listed around $7 by Food & Wine. Costco's own weekly warehouse page currently lists the muffins at $6.99.

For shoppers who prefer apple over pumpkin, Organic Granny Smith Apples are another seasonal option. The three- or four-pound bags are priced around $6 and are particularly useful for autumn baking, including apple pies and other desserts.

The bakery selection goes further with CT Bakery Apple Cider Cake Donuts, which cost about $7 for a dozen. The cinnamon-sugar-coated doughnuts can be warmed in the oven to give them a freshly baked feel.

There is also the Urban Bistro Apple Pie Squares With Cranberries, priced at around $11 for 10 pieces. Each individual pastry combines apple, cranberry and cinnamon flavors, offering a smaller dessert option than buying an entire pie.

Halloween treats and fall favorites worth checking out

Halloween shoppers have plenty of choices at Costco this October.

The Hershey's Assorted Bar Variety Pack includes 30 full-size candy bars and is currently listed at $19.99 after an October member discount, while the Haribo Gummi Candy Happy Mix contains 120 pieces and is priced at $9.99 during the promotion.

The offers are scheduled to run through October 18, although prices and availability can vary.

articles.body:
The latest Powerball winning numbers are the focus for lottery players across the United States as the jackpot climbs to an estimated $440 million for the Saturday, October 3, 2026 drawing.

However, the drawing has not yet taken place as of the time of publication. That means the official winning numbers for Saturday night are still pending and should not be confused with the numbers from Wednesday's previous draw.

The Powerball website confirms that the next drawing is scheduled for Saturday, October 3, at 10:59 p.m. ET, with an advertised jackpot of $440 million and a cash value of $181.3 million.

Once the drawing has been conducted, the winning combination will consist of five white-ball numbers from 1 through 69 and one red Powerball number from 1 through 26.

What were the previous Powerball winning numbers?

Wednesday's Powerball drawing, held on September 30, did not produce a jackpot winner. The official numbers were:

- White balls: 4, 6, 23, 33, 44

The official Powerball results show that nobody matched all five white balls and the Powerball. One ticket sold in Texas matched all five white balls without the Powerball and therefore won the $1 million second-tier prize.

The result was also reported by WKYC, which noted that the $409 million jackpot advertised for the September 30 drawing went unclaimed. That rollover subsequently increased the prize available for Saturday night.

The advertised jackpot for Saturday is $440 million if taken as an annuity. The alternative cash option is currently listed at $181.3 million on the official Powerball website.

There are also eight other prize levels, meaning players can win without hitting the jackpot. The Power Play option is available for an additional $1 and can increase eligible non-jackpot prizes.

Powerball drawings take place every Monday, Wednesday and Saturday at 10:59 p.m. ET at the Florida Lottery draw studio in Tallahassee. The official Powerball website also provides a live stream of the drawing.

Therefore, players looking for the October 3 Powerball winning numbers will need to wait until after Saturday night's drawing for the official result.

The numbers from September 30, 4, 6, 23, 33, 44 and Powerball 13, are the latest completed results, while the $440 million jackpot remains up for grabs until the October 3 numbers are drawn.

articles.body:
A plane with six people aboard lost contact during a flight from Bermuda to Boston, and the U.S. Coast Guard said it was searching early Saturday for the missing aircraft off the coast of Nantucket.

articles.title: Cornell 7: what to know about the investigation into Cornell University gang rape allegations
articles.standfirst: The case shocking America
articles.summary: The case shocking America
articles.body:
An intense, public outcry over a woman's account of being gang-raped at a Cornell University fraternity house prompted New York's governor this week to angrily yank control of the investigation away from the local prosecutor who didn't initially see what happened as a crime.

Tompkins County District Attorney Matthew Van Houten has said Cornell police omitted key information that could have affected his decision whether or not to pursue criminal charges.

Now, the task of unraveling the case will fall to the state's attorney general, Letitia James, who was appointed as a special prosecutor.

James, a Democrat best known for tangling with President Donald Trump, suggested at a news conference Friday that her investigation wouldn't be rushed. She described it as a monthslong process, with no predetermined outcome.

Here’s what we know and don’t know about the woman's allegations and the investigations that followed:

A lawsuit shone a fresh light on the woman's allegations

The woman sued Cornell and seven former students last month, alleging she was given ketamine and became completely incapacitated while members of the Chi Phi fraternity sexually assaulted her at their campus residence in October 2024.

She reported the alleged assault to campus police about three weeks later, giving investigators a detailed account over two days. She also spoke with Cornell’s disciplinary investigators.

But Van Houten quickly declined to pursue charges or further investigation after reviewing a police summary of her interview.

After the victim filed her civil suit, Van Houten said it contained allegations he had never seen. He contended Cornell’s police had withheld key information, including a transcript of the woman’s interview where she explicitly said she was “100% confident” she was raped.

Van Houten said the materials suggested she had consented to some sex with multiple men, hadn't been forced into other acts, and was intoxicated, but not to the point of helplessness.

Under New York law, being too drunk or high to consent to sex isn’t necessarily enough to support a rape charge. The law distinguishes that from being physically helpless or incapacitated by drugs administered without consent.

Van Houten later reopened the investigation. “Seeking justice sometimes requires us to reconsider or reopen cases when we are provided with additional evidence,” he said.

The school’s investigation produced conflicting accounts

Only a fraction of the evidence collected by the school has become public, but the portions that have provided a fuller — though disputed — timeline of events, as well as a glimpse at how the men responded to being accused.

According to the records, the woman had been invited to the fraternity by a member for whom she had long held strong romantic feelings. Cornell's disciplinary panel found that she initially consented to sex with that man and one of his friends, though she later alleged in her lawsuit that she had been pressured into taking drugs and alcohol and was too intoxicated to consent.

Later, other men started coming into the room, some drawn by a message one of the fraternity brothers sent to a Snapchat group at 1:42 a.m. using a vulgar term to advertise that a woman’s body was freely available.

The woman told investigators that her intoxication had rendered her partly defenseless. She said some of the men inhaled drugs off her unclothed body.

“I felt like bait. I felt like lions around me. It just was a totally debilitating place to be in,” she told investigators.

The records also show that she acknowledged that her memory of the night was spotty, due to her extreme inebriation, and had verbally acquiesced to some acts she later felt were sexual abuse.

Some of the accused men disputed her account when speaking to investigators, or said that the drug use and sexual activity were consensual.

Cornell hasn’t detailed the results of its investigation, but said it resulted in some students being expelled. The records show it also cleared at least some of the men of sexual assault allegations.

New York's governor was outraged by the police investigation

Hochul said she appointed James because she had lost faith in Van Houten's handling of the case. She said Van Houten should have asked Cornell for more information and interviewed the woman before closing it.

“This woman, this young woman, had already endured something that is utterly unspeakable,” she said. “And then at every turn, she was failed by people and institutions with an obligation to protect her.”

Van Houten said he supports James’ appointment but maintains that New York law didn’t allow him to prosecute based solely on the woman’s allegations that she was too incapacitated to consent.

The case sparks calls for change

At a Cornell Student Assembly meeting Thursday, students and other members of the university community spent more than 2 1/2 hours discussing the handling of sexual assault allegations. Some expressed fear, anger, and grief — while others shared their own experiences of sexual violence on campus.

Among them was Jane Wang, who said she had reported being sexually assaulted at Cornell a year earlier.

When she filed her Title IX case in the midst of “mental, physical and emotional recovery from the assault,” she said, “I was also met with an abundance of paperwork, very little instruction on how to navigate it and no follow-up from our Title IX office of an outcome.”

The presidents of every fraternity in Cornell’s Interfraternity Council voted unanimously to cancel social events this weekend in response to the allegations, according to The Cornell Daily Sun. Twenty student organizations are also planning a protest Monday calling for an independent review of Cornell’s handling of the case and changes to its sexual assault policies, the newspaper reported.

The case has also renewed scrutiny of a New York sexual assault law that makes it more difficult to prosecute cases involving people too intoxicated to consent. New York is one of 19 states with such laws.

Hochul said Friday that she supports changing the law.

articles.title: Christa Pike claims another victim after her botched execution
articles.standfirst: Governor says Tennessee's prisons chief is resigning
articles.summary: Governor says Tennessee's prisons chief is resigning
articles.body:
The head of Tennessee’s prison system is resigning after the failed execution of Christa Pike, Gov. Bill Lee announced Saturday.

Frank Strada, commissioner of the Department of Correction, will step down this month, Lee said.

Strada said in a statement that resigning was “in the best interest of Tennesseans” while an independent review determines what happened Wednesday when the state failed to execute Pike despite administering two doses of a lethal drug.

“I believe this review is entirely appropriate and necessary, and I look forward to doing everything I can to help determine exactly what occurred,” Strada said.

Pike was taken to a hospital, where she was on a ventilator and unconscious in the following hours, her attorneys said in a court filing Friday.

Hospital staff were working to save Pike’s life and, as of late Thursday, were trying to clear the two doses of pentobarbital, which the state uses to execute prisoners, lawyers said.

The stunning failure has left both sides of the death penalty debate demanding answers. Lee has ordered an independent review. Strada said he believes the state “carried out its responsibilities in accordance with the established protocol.”

Pike’s attorneys said they believed problems with the IV lines caused the pentobarbital to flow into her body instead of her bloodstream.

“Apparently at no point did any member of the execution team realize that the IV lines were not correctly placed or that the veins had blown and that the pentobarbital was, in whole or in part, entering Ms. Pike’s body,” they wrote in the court filing.

Strada took over the Correction Department in January 2023 after serving as deputy director of the Arizona Department of Corrections. In late 2024, he announced that Tennessee was changing its lethal injection protocol and would use only pentobarbital.

Pike was 18 when she and her boyfriend tortured and killed a classmate, Colleen Slemmer, in a jealous rage. She later became one of the youngest women to be sent to death row.

articles.title: Trump's $90 Medicare payment: who gets the check and when
articles.standfirst: The announcement comes just weeks before the November midterm elections
articles.summary: The announcement comes just weeks before the November midterm elections
articles.body:
P resident Donald Trump announced Friday that more than 20 million Americans enrolled in Medicare Part B will receive a one-time $90 payment this month to help offset the cost of their Medicare premiums. The White House said the payments will come from the Medicare Improvement Fund, which was established by Congress in 2008 to finance improvements to Medicare's traditional fee-for-service program.

The administration said the fund has about $2 billion available and that the payments represent the first time it has been used to directly provide money to Medicare beneficiaries. Most eligible beneficiaries will receive the $90 through direct deposit in early October.

Those without direct deposit will receive a paper check at the mailing address they have registered with Medicare. CMS said the vast majority of eligible beneficiaries should receive their direct deposits around Oct. 8, with some paper checks arriving later in the month.

Trump announced the payment in a Friday night post on Truth Social, describing the recipients as "wonderful Seniors" and saying the money would help with Medicare Part B premiums . The announcement comes just weeks before the November midterm elections and amid a series of administration proposals and payments aimed at reducing health care costs or putting money back into Americans' hands.

Who qualifies for the $90 payment?

According to the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services, the rebate is available to 20.8 million Americans enrolled in Original Medicare Part B who live in the United States and meet the program's eligibility requirements.

People whose Medicare premiums are already being paid by Medicaid are excluded. So are beneficiaries who pay an Income-Related Monthly Adjustment Amount, commonly known as IRMAA. Medicare Advantage enrollees are also not eligible for the payment.

The standard Medicare Part B premium in 2026 is $202.90 per month, meaning the $90 payment covers less than half of a standard monthly premium. For eligible seniors, however, the payment will arrive automatically rather than requiring a separate application. CMS said beneficiaries can call 1-800-MEDICARE at 1-800-633-4227 to check eligibility. Those seeking payment-status information can contact the Social Security Administration at 1-800-772-1213 beginning Oct. 15.

Where is the money coming from?

The payment is being funded through the Medicare Improvement Fund. The fund was created in 2008 to support improvements to Medicare Parts A and B. The White House says Congress p rovided approximately $2 billion for the fund but that no previous administration had used it to make direct payments to beneficiaries.

The Trump administration says previous congressional actions used money from the fund for other budget purposes. The White House specifically points to $20.7 billion that it says was withdrawn in connection with the Affordable Care Act in 2010.

Trump has argued that the money should instead be used to reduce costs for Medicare beneficiaries . The administration has also linked the payment to Trump's broader health care agenda, including efforts to reduce prescription-drug prices and other medical costs.

In announcing the checks, Trump said his administration was using the Medicare Improvement Fund along with his "Most Favored Nations" dru g-pricing agreements to lower costs for seniors. The White House has promoted those agreements as part of Trump's broader effort to bring U.S. prescription-drug prices closer to those paid in other countries.

Trump also used the announcement to renew his criticism of former President Joe Biden's administration and its handling of Medicare, Social Security and health care. Those political claims are disputed by Democrats, while the White House has presented the new payment as evidence that the administration is acting to reduce costs for seniors.

The payment is being funded through the Medicare Improvement Fund. The fund was created in 2008 to support improvements to Medicare Parts A and B. Trump also used the announcement to renew his criticism of former President Joe Biden's administration and its handling of Medicare, Social Security and health care. Those political claims are disputed by Democrats, while the White House has presented the new payment as evidence that the administration is acting to reduce costs for seniors.

articles.title: Christa Pike's second execution: What we know so far
articles.standfirst: The convicted killer remains critically ill as questions grow over whether Tennessee can attempt another execution
articles.summary: The convicted killer remains critically ill as questions grow over whether Tennessee can attempt another execution
articles.body:
Christa Pike remains critically ill after Tennessee's attempt to execute her by lethal injection failed, leaving questions over whether the state could ever try to carry out her death sentence again.

The 50-year-old was scheduled to be executed on September 30 at Riverbend Maximum Security Institution in Nashville. She was convicted of the 1995 torture and murder of 19-year-old Colleen Slemmer , a fellow Job Corps student.

Had the execution succeeded, Pike would've become the first woman executed by Tennessee in more than two centuries.

Instead, the execution went badly wrong. According to Pike's lawyers, members of the execution team struggled to establish intravenous access and used at least seven needles.

One needle was reportedly bent at a 90-degree angle. The state ultimately administered two doses of pentobarbital, but Pike survived. Her attorneys say the IV lines may have failed, allowing the drug to enter surrounding tissue instead of her bloodstream.

Witnesses reportedly heard Pike crying, whimpering and breathing heavily during the procedure. Her lawyers said she complained that her arm felt as though it was about to burst. When she reached the hospital, both arms were reportedly swollen, blistered and burned.

What happens if Pike survives?

Pike was unconscious and on a ventilator in a Nashville-area hospital as of October 2, with doctors working to treat the effects of the pentobarbital and save her life. Her attorneys have also asked Tennessee courts to preserve evidence connected to the failed execution.

The legal consequences could be complicated if Pike recovers. Her lawyers have already argued that the execution caused serious physical harm and have sought to protect her legal rights.

Questions could also arise over whether another execution attempt would violate constitutional protections against being punished twice, although the precise legal outcome isn't settled.

Her medical condition could become another important factor.

“She can’t be executed if she is brain injured and doesn’t understand the proceedings,” Professor Deborah Dunno told the New York Post.

“The United States Supreme Court recognized in a case involving a dementia patient in 2019 that you can’t execute someone who’s not aware of the punishment that they’re going to receive.”

At this time Tennessee isn't preparing another execution date. Governor Bill Lee has suspended executions for the remainder of 2026 while an independent review examines what went wrong.

The fallout has already reached the state's prison leadership. Frank Strada , commissioner of the Tennessee Department of Correction, is stepping down later this month as the investigation continues.

Strada said the department had followed established procedures, while acknowledging that his departure was in the state's best interest.

Pike's future therefore remains uncertain. Her recovery, the findings of Tennessee's investigation and subsequent court proceedings could all determine whether her death sentence remains enforceable and whether another execution attempt can take place.

articles.title: Cibelle Savella's ex-husband breaks his silence following the brutal murder of his daughter Vivian in Texas
articles.standfirst: Four-year-old was expected to return to her father hours before fatal shooting
articles.summary: Four-year-old was expected to return to her father hours before fatal shooting
articles.body:
A Texas father is grieving the death of his four-year-old daughter after she was fatally shot in her Houston home in an apparent murder-suicide involving her mother, just hours after a family court hearing over the child's custody.

Vivian Savella was expected to return to her father, Aaron Savella, on the evening of the shooting. Instead, Houston police found the young girl dead inside a west Houston home after responding to reports of gunfire at about 5:45 p.m.

Police said Vivian had suffered an apparent gunshot wound. Her mother, 35-year-old Cibelle Savella , was also found with a gunshot wound and was taken to a hospital. Authorities later confirmed that Cibelle died from her injuries.

The deaths came on the same day as a custody hearing involving Vivian . According to the family's attorney and sources cited by ABC13, a judge had awarded primary custody of the child to Aaron . Court documents also indicated that Cibelle's visits with Vivian were to take place only under continuous supervision.

In a statement released through attorney Stefani Shapiro, Aaron's family said Vivian was deeply loved and described the loss as devastating.

“Our family is devastated. Vivian was four years old. She was loved without limit by her father, Aaron, and by everyone whose life she touched. There are no words for what has been taken from us,” read the statement.

“Aaron did everything the law asks of a parent who is trying to protect his child. He trusted the courts. He followed every order. He waited for the process to work. On Tuesday, a judge placed Vivian in his primary care, and she was supposed to come home to him that evening. She never did.”

The attorney said Aaron had never accused Cibelle of physically abusing Vivian , but had expressed concerns about possible emotional abuse. The family's statement emphasized that Aaron had pursued the matter through the court system rather than outside it.

Custody ruling preceded the devastating shooting

The former couple divorced in November 2024 after four years of marriage, according to reports, and their separation was followed by a contentious dispute over Vivian's care.

The latest court order gave Aaron primary custody and exclusive authority over important decisions concerning his daughter, according to reporting based on court documents. Cibelle's contact with Vivian was restricted, and the supervision requirement was expected to be handled by a court-appointed agency.

Other reported restrictions included limits on Cibelle's involvement in Vivian's school activities and medical decisions. Reports also said that communication in Portuguese, Cibelle's native language, was subject to supervision by someone able to understand the language.

At the Houston residence when the gunfire erupted were Cibelle's husband and a childcare aide. Investigators spoke with both people as part of the inquiry, and they aren't believed to have been involved in the shootings.

Houston police continue to investigate the circumstances surrounding the deaths. While the shooting happened shortly after the custody hearing, authorities haven't publicly established a definitive motive or said that the court ruling itself caused the violence.

articles.title: In 2015, a man began building a train line in his backyard: after 18,000 kilos of gravel and 120 meters of track, his neighbors line up to use it
articles.standfirst: Cory Mohl needed an investment of $18,000
articles.summary: Cory Mohl needed an investment of $18,000
articles.body:
Building a railroad track in your backyard may seem like an impossible idea. For Cory Mohl , however, it was the way to turn a lifelong hobby into a reality. In 2015 , this resident of West Valley City, Utah, decided to undertake a project as unusual as it was ambitious: to build his own garden railroad.

What started as a personal project ended up becoming an attraction for the whole neighborhood. To make it a reality, Mohl had to move around 18,000 kilos of gravel and spend hundreds of hours preparing the ground, laying the tracks, and getting the little train up and running.

The route extends about 120 meters and winds through the property’s grounds, even including a section that passes through a shed. It was not simply a matter of laying decorative rails: the infrastructure had to support a train that other people could ride.

From personal hobby to neighborhood attraction

Mohl had been fascinated by trains for years and had devoted part of his time to building model railways. When his daughter grew up and became more independent, he found the perfect moment to take that passion to a completely different scale.

The work required planning, physical effort, and numerous weekends. Gravel was needed to create a stable base on which to install the track, while the rails, sleepers, and switches had to be properly aligned to ensure that the train could run.

And then something happened that Mohl probably did not expect at first

When the line was operational, the neighborhood children started asking for rides, and the railroad ceased to be merely an enthusiast's project. The backyard was transformed into a small improvised station where family members and neighbors could enjoy a train ride without leaving the neighborhood.

The cost was also considerable. Mohl estimated that the total investment would end up standing at between $17,500 and $18,000 , an amount that included materials, equipment, and the rolling stock itself.

Far from considering the project finished, the owner planned to keep expanding it and add new decorative elements . Thus, what began as an extravagant idea in 2015 ended up proving that a backyard can become, with enough patience and passion, a railway capable of sparking the curiosity of an entire neighborhood.

articles.title: A uranium processing plant left radioactive waste for decades in a Colorado river: since 2009, more than 17 million tons have been removed by train
articles.standfirst: A mountain of waste beside the river
articles.summary: A mountain of waste beside the river
articles.body:
For decades, a huge mountain of radioactive waste remained just a few meters from the Colorado River . Its origin was an old uranium processing plant located near Moab , in Utah , and removing that nuclear legacy has become one of the great environmental cleanup operations in the United States .

Since 2009, trains have transported more than 17 million tons of uranium waste to a disposal site located approximately 30 miles from the original site. The goal is to move this material away from the river and prevent the contaminants from continuing to pose a threat to the environment.

The problem began more than half a century ago

The Moab plant began operating in 1956 , during the expansion of the uranium industry in the Cold War . There, ore was processed to obtain uranium concentrate, leaving behind enormous amounts of waste known as tailings.

When the facility closed, those residues remained piled up next to the Colorado River. The problem was not only the size of the artificial mountain. The contaminants could reach the groundwater , while the river’s proximity made any movement of the materials an environmental concern.

Now, the landscape is changing thanks to an operation that uses the railroad as a fundamental component. The waste is removed, conditioned, and loaded onto railcars to make the journey to Crescent Junction. There, it is stored in a facility specially designed to isolate it and reduce the risk of water or erosion dispersing it.

Not everything is done yet at the Moab mill

The volume already removed gives an idea of the scale of the problem: 17 million tons are equivalent to a gigantic amount of material that for decades remained next to one of the most important rivers in the western United States.

But there is still work to be done. The operation also includes the recovery of affected land and measures aimed at controlling groundwater contamination.

The U.S. Department of Energy expects to complete the main tasks of the project in 2029 . Until then, trains will continue removing from the former site waste that remained there for decades.

The cleanup of Moab is, ultimately, the slow dismantling of a legacy from the nuclear era: a mountain of waste that for years was part of the Colorado River landscape and is now disappearing car by car.

articles.title: A 12-year-old girl was fatally shot at Baltimore park where youth football game was
articles.standfirst: The victim's identity is unknown at this time
articles.summary: The victim's identity is unknown at this time
articles.body:
A 12-year-old girl was killed when she was caught in the crossfire of gunshots between two men who apparently were arguing over a parking space in a Baltimore park where a youth football game was being played, police said.

Officers responded to Leon Day Park at 6:15 p.m. Saturday, where the girl and a woman were found with gunshot wounds. Two men also walked into area hospitals seeking treatment, Baltimore Police Commissioner Richard Worley said at a news conference.

The girl was pronounced dead at a hospital. The three adults suffered injuries that weren’t life-threatening, Worley said.

Two men involved in an argument believed to be over a parking spot began shooting at each other, and the girl and the woman were struck by bullets, Worley said. He said police were seeking “at least” two suspects.

Worley said the girl wasn't a direct target of the shooting.

“What we know is there was some type of argument between two cowards,” Worley said. “They both opened fire on each other. In the crossfire, a 12-year-old little girl, who was probably down there watching football, was shot and killed.”

Police were still processing the scene in the expansive park, and Worley said it wasn't immediately known how many shots were fired. He urged anyone who witnessed the shooting to contact police.

“Two grown men got into an argument, and now a 12-year-old is gone,” Baltimore Mayor Brandon Scott said at the news conference. “We never should have to say something like that. What happened out here today is one of the most disgusting things I’ve ever seen in my life."

articles.title: Under strict surveillance and intubated: Inside Christa Pike's hospital room after failed execution in Tennessee
articles.summary: Christa Pike’s failed execution has now become a medical and legal crisis, with her attorneys saying they still don't know whether she will recover from the effects of two doses of pentobarbital administered by the state.
articles.body:
C hrista Pike ’s failed execution has now become a medical and legal crisis, with her attorneys saying they still don't know whether she will recover from the effects of two doses of pentobarbital administered by the state.

Assistant Federal Defender Stephen Ferrell said Sunday that Pike , 50, remains hospitalized on a ventilator and under guard.

Asked whether she had regained consciousness since the execution attempt, Ferrell told CNN’s State of the Union: “Not that I am aware of.

“She is guarded. I’m not sure who may have seen her. I know I have not seen her.”

He added that Tennessee hasn't said whether it would try to execute Pike again if she survives.

Pike may never fully recover

Ferrell said the uncertainty surrounding Pike ’s condition could last for days, particularly because doctors are still trying to determine the long-term effects of the pentobarbital.

“I think one of the main things that will leave this up in the air for a while is the fact that we don’t know what the prognosis is, as in the long term prognosis,” he said. He also warned that Pike “may not fully recover.”

Witnesses to the execution attempt said Pike appeared to be in severe pain in one arm before losing consciousness. Her attorneys later said her arms were burned and blistered after the lethal injection process.

“We don’t know right now, and we may never know what sort of torture she endured during that process, where her consciousness was, what physical pain there was, what mental torture she went through,” Ferrell said.

Pike had previously assigned medical power of attorney to another person, who is now making decisions about her care. Her legal team has not identified that person publicly.

Tennessee execution system comes under renewed scrutiny

The failed execution has also intensified scrutiny of Tennessee’s death penalty procedures.

Pike ’s execution was delayed for more than eight hours while the U.S. Supreme Court considered a lower-court ruling that temporarily halted the process. The Supreme Court ultimately overturned that ruling, allowing the execution to proceed.

Her lawyers have since asked a court to order Tennessee officials to preserve all records, communications, images and video connected to the execution attempt.

“The state of Tennessee has got to start telling its people exactly what it is doing so that in the democratic process, the people of Tennessee can decide if that’s what they want to be done in their name,” Ferrell added.

The incident follows another failed execution attempt in May, when Tennessee stopped the execution of Tony Carruthers after staff couldn't establish a secondary IV line.

Gov. Bill Lee has now ordered an independent investigation into the state’s capital punishment system. Pike was sentenced to death for the 1995 killing of 19-year-old Colleen Slemmer.

Her lawyers are asking that her sentence be commuted to life imprisonment. If she survives, the question of whether Tennessee seeks another execution date remains unresolved.

articles.title: The needle burst her vein! Leaked photo reveals Christa Pike's horrific injuries following botched execution
articles.standfirst: A prison source claims the lethal injection needle damaged a vein, sending chemicals into surrounding muscle
articles.summary: A prison source claims the lethal injection needle damaged a vein, sending chemicals into surrounding muscle
articles.body:
Questions surrounding Christa Pike ’s failed execution are growing after a photograph reportedly taken after the procedure showed extensive bruising and discoloration along one of her arms.

The image, which RadarOnline.com obtained but declined to publish, was said to have come from inside the Tennessee Department of Correction . A prison-connected source offered a specific explanation for the injury.

“The needle blew her vein, causing the chemicals to go to the muscle,” the source said.

That account adds to concerns already raised by Pike ’s attorneys over the way the lethal injection was administered.

Pike , 50, remains hospitalized after receiving two doses of pentobarbital during the failed execution attempt.

Attorneys describe severe injuries after lethal injection

Pike ’s legal team has said she arrived at the hospital with arms that were “swollen, burned, and blistered” after multiple attempts to establish IV access.

Witnesses described Pike crying out during the procedure and complaining of intense pain in her arm.

“Does this happen like that?” she reportedly asked. At another point, she said, “My arm feels like it’s about to burst open.”

The prison source who provided the photo to RadarOnline.com also claimed Pike showed “stroke-like symptoms,” prompting concern about possible neurological damage.

No official medical finding confirming permanent brain injury has been released.

Tennessee anesthesiologist Dr. Paul Allen has suggested that improper needle placement could explain some of the reported injuries, noting that dehydration can make IV access more difficult.

The exact cause of Pike ’s injuries remains under investigation.

Mounting pressure for Tennessee execution system

The fallout has already reached the highest levels of Tennessee’s corrections system.

Frank Strada , commissioner of the Tennessee Department of Correction, resigned three days after the failed execution.

Gov. Bill Lee said the decision was in the “best interest of Tennesseans” and ordered an independent review of the state’s execution procedures.

“Carrying out a lawfully imposed sentence is among the State’s most serious responsibilities,” Lee said.

Scheduled executions have also been halted for the remainder of the year while the review takes place.

Pike ’s case is the second execution-related failure in Tennessee this year, deepening questions about how lethal injection procedures are being carried out and what safeguards exist when complications develop.

The state has maintained that approved protocols were followed. Pike ’s attorneys argue the episode points to a broader problem.

“What happened to her reflects a systemic failure that goes far beyond any one person,” they said. “We need a thorough investigation into these profound issues.”
